title: Spatial distribution of gamma radiation dose rates from natural radionuclides and its radiological hazards in sediments along river Iju, Ogun state Nigeria
author: Maxwell, Olusegun O., et al.
materials: Dependent and Independent Variables for the Statistical Analysis

steps.title: Collect sediment samples
steps.instruction: At 13 pre‑selected sites along the Iju River, scoop sediment from a depth of 10 cm to obtain ~1000 g per site, spacing the sites ~50 m apart and targeting locations used by local communities for water use.

steps.title: Air‑dry samples
steps.instruction: Spread the collected sediments in a clean tray and air‑dry at ambient temperature (≈29 °C) for one week.

steps.title: Crush, powder and oven‑dry
steps.instruction: Crush each air‑dried sample and grind to a maximum grain size of 1 mm. Transfer ~500 g of the powdered material to a drying oven set to approximately 105 °C and dry until a constant weight is reached.

steps.title: Seal samples for transport and equilibrium
steps.instruction: Place each oven‑dry sample into a high‑density polyethylene bottle, label clearly, and seal in a radon‑impermeable plastic container for 4 weeks to allow Rn‑222 and its short‑lived daughters to reach equilibrium with Ra‑226. Ship the sealed bottles to the Activation Analysis Laboratory in Canada for gamma counting.

steps.title: Gamma‑spectroscopy measurement
steps.instruction: Measure each sample with a NaI(Tl) detector (3" × 3") equipped with lead shielding that reduces background by ~95 %. Count each sample for 21 000 s. Record the photopeak areas for the following energies: 1.46 MeV (K‑40), 1.76 MeV (Bi‑214, proxy for U‑238), and 2.614 MeV (Tl‑208, proxy for Th‑232). The detector detection limits are 8.50 Bq kg⁻¹ for K‑40, 2.21 Bq kg⁻¹ for U‑238 and 2.11 Bq kg⁻¹ for Th‑232.

steps.title: Calculate activity concentrations
steps.instruction: Use the following equation to compute the activity concentration (Cs, Bq kg⁻¹) of each radionuclide in the sediment:

substeps.instruction: Cs = Cref · Ps · Ds − Pb · Db · (Pref · Dref − Pb · Db) · Ms
Cs = activity concentration of the sample
Cref = activity concentration of the reference material
Ps, Pref, Pb = photopeak areas of sample, reference material and background (dimensionless)
Ds, Dref, Db = counting times (seconds) for sample, reference material and background

steps.title: Determine measurement uncertainty
steps.instruction: Calculate the combined uncertainty (Q) of each activity concentration using:

substeps.instruction: QCref = relative uncertainty of the reference material
Qs, Qref, Qb = count‑rate uncertainties of sample, reference material and background
Rs, Rref, Rb = net counts of the radionuclide line for sample, reference material and background

steps.title: Interpolate spatial dose rates
steps.instruction: Import the measured gamma dose‑rate values into ArcGIS 10.8 and apply an Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) interpolation to generate a spatial distribution map of dose rates across the Iju River sediments.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of radionuclide data
steps.instruction: Perform two‑way ANOVA in Excel to assess variation among sites and sampling days, then conduct multiple linear regression in R‑Studio 3.0.2:

substeps.instruction: Convert categorical variables (site, day) to dummy variables (0 or 1) in Excel.
Import the dummy‑coded dataset into R‑Studio.
Fit separate regression models for U‑238, Th‑232 and K‑40 using the dummy variables as predictors.
Report ANOVA tables, regression coefficients, p‑values, and model statistics (e.g., adjusted R²).
